findings.observation: The original production guard allowed all java.. dependencies. A compiled application/MutationProbe.java field of java.sql.Connection passed the same production guard (2 tests, zero failures).
findings.consequence: The fixture could report a green structural check while its persistence-independent core directly depended on JDBC.
findings.correction: Compose the original package allowlist with an explicit prohibition of java.sql.. and javax.sql..; add a separate hostile JDBC class and test using that same composed rule. Preserve the independent Spring hostile control and production coverage checks.

findings.observation: Guidance already asked for Spring/JDBC/adapter sensitivity controls but did not identify the Java-package allowance trap illustrated by its own fixture.
findings.consequence: A Spring-only negative control could leave a consequential independent allowance untested.
findings.correction: Explain narrow allowances versus explicit JDBC exclusions, require independent framework/JDBC controls for the promised boundary, and qualify the check as dependency-policy evidence rather than proof of absence of all I/O.
Record the current 17-test suite and actual JDBC before/after/restoration experiment; retain the prior five mutations and 16-test results as earlier evidence, explicitly not rerun this time.

limits: Dependency rules cover the explicitly selected packages and static dependencies. The Java allowance does not prove absence of all I/O, reflection, dynamic bean selection or other side effects.
Fixture evidence is Java 25/Boot 4.1.1/ArchUnit 1.5.0 in this environment; no target production application or other JDK/framework baseline was exercised.
H2 and MockMvc tests do not establish another database's SQL/isolation, actual credential validation, a live TCP path, concurrency safety or distributed durability.
The five pre-existing historical mutations were preserved as prior evidence, not rerun. Current full suite and targeted JDBC before/after mutation were run.
Development cases below are not held-out or independently executed agent evaluations.
Global index regeneration and repository verification are deferred to coordinator by parallel ownership rules.
